chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab; and my father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is [the reward] for one who visits one of you [one of you]?' He replied, '[It is] like [the reward of] one who visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) establishes the profound spiritual equivalence between visiting the Imams and visiting the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.), affirming their status as the living continuation of prophetic guidance. This concept underscores the Shia belief that the Imams are the true heirs of the Prophet’s authority and knowledge, making their visitation a means of drawing closer to the divine source. The hadith serves as a foundational text for the practice of Ziyarah, emphasizing that honoring the Ahl al-Bayt is intrinsically linked to honoring the Messenger of Allah.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Muḥammad ibn Ya’qūb Al-Kulayni narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of one of you (the Imams (a.s.))?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “They are like those who have gone to the Ziyārah of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.).” The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from Sāliḥ ibn ‘Uqbah, from Zayd Al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
